title: Out-of-Band Sensor Threshold Breach (IPMI)
exclusions: Reports a valid IPMI threshold sensor whose BMC status is lower/upper non-critical, critical, or non-recoverable. It does not compare only upper limits, apply one unit or numeric threshold across temperature/voltage/fan/current sensors, treat `ns`/unreadable as healthy, monitor discrete non-threshold sensors, prove current workload impact, or diagnose cooling, power, board, sensor, or environmental cause. Redfish Sensor data can implement an equivalent separately qualified contract but is not mixed silently with IPMI abbreviations. Missing expected sensors, invalid readings, threshold absence, stale polls, SEL events, and collector failure are separate controls. Vendor thresholds and status are observed facts; the five-minute cadence, severity, retention, and exceptions are local policy. No fan/power/thermal control is changed.
evidence: After deployment, retain chassis/BMC and expected-sensor inventory; BMC/IPMI/tool/firmware versions; credential/network policy; collector/parser/input revision; representative raw `ipmitool sensor -c`/SDR output and units; mapping for `lnr/lcr/lnc/unc/ucr/unr/ok/ns`; expected-sensor, invalid-read, threshold, staleness, and poll health; version-controlled `ipmi_sensor_threshold_breach` search, ACL, schedule, dispatches, and rows; BMC UI/SEL/facility/workload corroboration and disposition; and dated all-six-status, OK, NS, lower-fan, upper-temperature, null-threshold, unit, duplicate, stale, recovery, and routing tests. This documentation-only review polled no BMC and validated no production sensor.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed completed 15-minute window, ingest the newest valid sample for `host=server01`, `sensor_id=FAN1`, `sensor_type=Fan`, `reading=300`, `units=RPM`, and `threshold_status=lcr`; expect one critical row preserving lower thresholds and source identity. Repeat `unc` for a temperature sensor and expect high, and `unr` for voltage and expect critical. Assert status, reading, all available thresholds, units, event/index times, and `use_case=UC-1.4.9`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero breach rows for newest `threshold_status=ok`; for an old breach followed by newer OK; wrong source/type; blank host/sensor ID; unsupported status; invalid/nonnumeric reading; duplicate; or out-of-window record. Separately prove `ns`, unreadable/disabled scanning, missing expected sensor, absent thresholds, poll/credential/network failure, unit drift, and stale sample create source-health findings and cannot be represented as OK.

dataSources: A read-only management-network collector runs qualified `ipmitool sensor -c`/SDR queries and emits `index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:ipmi_sensor` with managed `host`, `bmc`, stable `sensor_id`, name/type, numeric `reading`, `units`, canonical `threshold_status` (`lnr`, `lcr`, `lnc`, `ok`, `unc`, `ucr`, `unr`, or `ns`), each available lower/upper threshold, reading-valid/scanning flags, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Preserve raw CSV/SDR identity and command status. Redfish Sensor `Reading`, `ReadingUnits`, `Thresholds`, and Status can feed a separate normalized implementation after field-by-field qualification.
app: A deployment-owned Splunk app containing a least-privilege IPMI/Redfish sensor collector, parser and field contract, expected-sensor/source-health searches, saved search, fixtures, exact maintenance lookup, dashboard, and runbook. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux does not define this BMC sensor schema, and Universal Forwarder is not Splunkbase app 617.
spl:
index=hardware sourcetype=hardware:ipmi_sensor earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval endpoint=lower(trim(host)), sensor=lower(trim(sensor_id)), threshold_state=lower(trim(threshold_status)), numeric_reading=tonumber(reading)
| where len(endpoint)>0 AND len(sensor)>0 AND isnotnull(numeric_reading)
| sort 0 endpoint sensor -_time -_indextime
| dedup endpoint sensor
| where threshold_state IN ("lnr","lcr","lnc","unc","ucr","unr")
| eval severity=if(threshold_state IN ("lnr","lcr","ucr","unr"),"critical","high"), direction=if(substr(threshold_state,1,1)="l","lower","upper"), class=case(match(threshold_state,"nr$"),"non_recoverable",match(threshold_state,"cr$"),"critical",true(),"non_critical"), event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), indexed_time=strftime(_indextime,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), use_case="UC-1.4.9"
| table event_time indexed_time endpoint bmc sensor sensor_name sensor_type numeric_reading units threshold_state direction class severity lower_non_recoverable lower_critical lower_non_critical upper_non_critical upper_critical upper_non_recoverable source_record use_case
| sort 0 -severity endpoint sensor
description: Reports the newest valid BMC threshold-sensor sample when IPMI marks any lower or upper non-critical, critical, or non-recoverable state. The rule preserves reading, unit, direction, class, and all available thresholds, so a low fan speed is handled as correctly as a high temperature without inventing universal values.
value: Out-of-band sensors can reveal cooling, power, voltage, current, or board conditions even when the operating system is unavailable. Using the BMC's actual threshold-state bits and component identity speeds safe verification while avoiding a one-sided upper-limit rule that misses low fan/voltage conditions or compares unlike units.
implementation: Inventory expected threshold sensors per supported BMC, qualify read-only IPMI status abbreviations, validity flags, units, and all six threshold fields, then poll every five minutes with bounded timeout. Build missing/invalid/stale health separately, save the delayed latest-state breach search, test every state and recovery against raw output and BMC UI, and route with chassis, sensor, facility, workload, and change context.
visualization: Lead with expected-sensor coverage, invalid/NS readings, poll freshness, and unit/threshold completeness. Show breached sensors by chassis/type/status with reading and same-unit lower/upper thresholds, a timechart per sensor with labeled limits, BMC SEL/facility/change overlays, and raw drilldown. Never combine unlike units on one gauge or show missing sensors as green.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable — no CIM data model for IPMI SDR fields.

knownFalsePositives:
A row is a genuine BMC-reported threshold state, but it may be expected, transient, stale, or mis-normalized.

1. **Approved thermal/power/fan test** — diagnostics or facility failover can intentionally cross a threshold. Match exact chassis/sensor/test/change, owner, expected direction/status, bounded interval, stop criteria, and recovery.

2. **Boot, firmware update, or fan spin-up transition** — sensors can briefly cross lower fan or voltage limits during supported lifecycle. Confirm exact event sequence, BMC UI/SEL, sample age, workload state, and recovery; do not suppress all boot periods.

3. **Sensor/unit/parser mismatch** — OEM SDR changes can rename sensors, change units/scaling, or return `ns`. Compare raw output and BMC UI on the exact firmware; invalid/NS remains source health, not OK.

4. **Threshold policy intentionally changed** — vendor/BMC configuration can alter thresholds. Reconcile and approve the change; never overwrite indexed thresholds with a generic fleet value.

5. **Stale BMC reading** — communication or BMC sensor-scan failure can leave an old breached sample. Display age and scan validity, and investigate source health before repeated paging.

6. **Facility condition without server impact** — a genuine inlet temperature or input-voltage breach may recover before workload degradation. Preserve it and correlate facility/PDU/workload evidence rather than relabeling it false.

Suppress notification only by exact chassis/sensor/status with owner, reason, change, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress invalid/NS, missing expected sensor, threshold/unit drift, stale/no poll, or collector health.
detectionType: vendor-reported IPMI lower or upper threshold state
hardware: Physical servers/appliances with an IPMI or qualified Redfish BMC exposing threshold sensors. Preserve chassis, BMC, sensor/SDR identity, physical context, units, firmware, expected-sensor inventory, rack/facility/PDU mapping, workload, and owner; threshold availability and semantics vary by platform.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact threshold contract

Assign datacenter/facilities, hardware/BMC, server/workload, Splunk data/content, and incident owners. Inventory every supported chassis/BMC and expected threshold sensor with SDR/sensor ID, name/type, physical context, units, valid lower/upper thresholds, firmware/tool version, rack/PDU/facility mapping, workload, and owner. Use a least-privilege read-only BMC account over the management network; never expose command-line passwords or grant fan, power, threshold-write, reset, or host-control privilege. This review ran no BMC and asserts no version compatibility.

IPMI threshold states cover Lower Non-Recoverable (`lnr`), Lower Critical (`lcr`), Lower Non-Critical (`lnc`), Upper Non-Critical (`unc`), Upper Critical (`ucr`), and Upper Non-Recoverable (`unr`). `ok` is normal; `ns`/invalid means not specified/readable, not normal. This is why comparing only reading >= upper thresholds is factually incomplete: low fan speed or voltage can breach lower limits. Use the BMC-returned threshold status after platform qualification and preserve values/units.

## Step 1 — Collect valid, unit-bearing samples

From a hardened collector, run a machine-readable qualified `ipmitool sensor -c` or equivalent SDR/sensor query under bounded timeout. Parse fields by tested CSV behavior, not visual column spacing. Emit managed host/BMC, stable sensor ID/name/type, numeric reading, units, canonical threshold status, all six available threshold values, reading-valid and scanning/event flags, raw source identity, tool/firmware/parser version, command status/duration, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Retain raw evidence access-restricted.

For Redfish, discover Chassis Sensors and map `Reading`, `ReadingUnits`, `Thresholds.LowerCaution/LowerCritical/LowerFatal/UpperCaution/UpperCritical/UpperFatal`, and Status under a separate qualified parser. DMTF requires thresholds to use the reading's units, but IPMI and Redfish severity names are not identical; test mapping before combining output.

Poll every five minutes only after measuring BMC load and runtime. Limit concurrency/jitter fleet polls. Maintain independent expected-sensor and collector health: no poll, missing/unexpected sensor, `ns`/invalid/unavailable reading, scanning disabled, null/nonnumeric reading, missing/changed unit or thresholds, duplicate ID/route, stale/future time, auth/network/timeout error, parser/schema drift, and index delay. Silence cannot mean OK.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the SPL

Save sidecar SPL as `ipmi_sensor_threshold_breach`. Run every 15 minutes over `earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m`, a complete 15-minute slice after measured five-minute allowance. The search validates identity and numeric reading, sorts newest first, keeps one sample per host/sensor, and selects exactly the six threshold states. Lower/upper direction is derived from the first character; nonrecoverable/critical states route critical and noncritical states high as local policy. It reports the BMC state rather than recalculating with possibly null thresholds. `ok`, `ns`, missing, and unknown states are not alert rows; the latter three remain health findings.

## Step 3 — Validate every direction and failure mode

Replay fixed raw/normalized fixtures for lnr/lcr/lnc/ok/unc/ucr/unr/ns; temperature, fan, voltage, current, power, and platform-specific units; null unavailable thresholds; zero/negative/decimal values; reading invalid; scanning disabled; duplicate sensor names with distinct IDs; duplicate routes; stale/out-of-order/late events; old breach followed by OK; and exact dispatch boundaries. Assert lower fan and upper temperature cases retain correct direction/threshold/unit.

In a disposable lab, compare collector output with raw IPMI and the vendor BMC UI/Redfish Sensor resource. Use vendor-supported sensor simulation or carefully governed thermal/fan/power tests only with facilities approval, redundancy, workload protection, stop criteria, out-of-band access, and rollback. Never disconnect cooling or power on production solely to test. Capture SEL, facility/PDU and workload evidence plus recovery. Keep draft until owners approve mappings, fixtures, inventory, source health, timing, dashboard, alert routes, and response.

## Step 4 — Operationalize without unsafe control

Alert text states `BMC reports <sensor> <threshold status>` and includes chassis/BMC, sensor/type/physical context, reading/unit, crossed direction/class and same-unit thresholds, event/index age, source validity, related SEL/facility/change, workload, and owner. Responders verify raw reading/status and current BMC UI; check nearby sensors and facility/PDU state; inspect fans, airflow, filters, temperature, voltage/power, board and firmware according to vendor procedure; assess workload; and escalate. Never change thresholds/fan curves, override controls, reset BMC, power-cycle, or move workload automatically from one reading.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and close

- **Only `ns`:** inspect reading-valid/scanning flags, sensor type/SDR support, BMC firmware, tool version and permissions. Keep coverage unhealthy.
- **Lower breaches missing:** verify parser preserves lnr/lcr/lnc and search does not only evaluate upper fields.
- **Reading and threshold units disagree:** stop numeric interpretation, inspect raw SDR/parser/scaling, and requalify against BMC UI.
- **Many sensors breach together:** examine facility inlet/cooling/power, BMC restart, parser scaling, and shared chassis cause before treating them independently.
- **Old breach persists:** check poll freshness, BMC sensor scan, event/index time, collector errors, and current UI; do not erase historical evidence.
- **Redfish/IPMI differ:** align sensor identity, timestamps, units, severity mapping, and firmware. They may expose different abstractions; keep them separate until parity is proven.

Close after current sensor and collection health are normal or an approved accepted state exists, facility/hardware/workload impact and cause are documented, remediation/change evidence is linked, and bounded exceptions expire.
grandmaExplanation: We read the safe limits that the server's own controller reports for each temperature, fan, voltage, or similar sensor. We catch readings that are too low as well as too high and keep the units clear.
